div.head: About the Edition
div.p: Probstücke Digital is a digital edition of the 24 Prob-Stücke (test pieces) that form the “Ober-Classe” of Johann Mattheson’s thoroughbass treatise. Each Prob-Stück is a figured bass, one in each of the 24 keys, followed by Mattheson’s Erläuterung: a commentary that discusses individual bars and often shows in a short music example how the right hand might be realised.

Mattheson published the treatise twice: as Exemplarische Organisten-Probe im Artikel vom General-Bass (Hamburg: Schiller und Kißner, 1719) and, revised and enlarged, as Grosse General-Baß-Schule (Hamburg: Kißner, 1731). The edition presents both versions, so that Mattheson’s revisions of the music and of the commentary can be followed piece by piece.

list.item: The figured basses of all 24 Prob-Stücke, encoded in MEI. One encoding per piece records both prints. Where they differ, both readings are encoded, and each page shows the reading of the print it belongs to.
Diplomatic transcriptions of Mattheson’s commentary from both prints, encoded in TEI: 23 from 1719 and 24 from 1731. For Probstück 24 only the 1731 commentary is included.
An English translation of the commentary by Niels Pfeffer, made from the 1731 text.

Lessons and realisations: two lessons that Robert Hill gave on Probstücke 3 and 4 at the Hochschule für Musik Freiburg in May 2019, transcribed from audio recordings, and a realisation of Probstück 4 by Dijoux with notes in French.
Editorial notes, and indices of the persons, literature and musical works mentioned in the commentary, linked to the Integrated Authority File (GND) where possible.

div.head: Sources
div.p: The transcriptions and the page images are based on copies in the Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, Munich:

list.item: 1719: Exemplarische Organisten-Probe, shelfmark Mus.th. 977 a. Digital copy · Catalogue record
1731: Grosse General-Baß-Schule, shelfmark Mus.th. 978 a. Digital copy · Catalogue record

div.p: Page images are loaded directly from the library’s IIIF service. Each line of music in the edition is linked to the corresponding area of the page in both prints.

div.head: Selection
div.p: Both versions of the treatise consist of a theoretical preparation, 24 easier examples and the 24 more difficult Prob-Stücke. The edition covers the Prob-Stücke with their commentaries. The preparation and the easier examples are not included.

div.head: Editorial Approach
div.p: Music and text are encoded following the standards of the Music Encoding Initiative (MEI) and the Text Encoding Initiative (TEI). The commentary is transcribed diplomatically following the Base Format of the Deutsches Textarchiv (DTABf), preserving original spelling, line beginnings, catchwords and page breaks. The rules are described in the editorial guidelines.

For easier reading, the website shows the 1719 and 1731 commentaries in modernised spelling. The modernisation is produced automatically by CAB, the normalisation service of the Deutsches Textarchiv, and has not been checked word by word. Point at a word to see its original spelling. The diplomatic transcription itself is contained in the TEI files, which can be downloaded from every page.

div.head: Reading the Edition
div.p: On each page the score is on the left and the commentary on the right. Highlighted passages in the commentary refer to bars, notes or figures in the score: point at a passage to see them marked in the score, or at a marked element in the score to find the passage. Point at a line of music to see it in the original print. The buttons above the score switch between original and modern clefs, show or hide the upper staff with the right-hand passages notated in the print, and add or remove empty staves for writing out a realisation.
